skill.name: setup-dev-env
skill.description: Guides a full-stack development environment setup with Java, Gradle, pnpm, Docker Compose, PostgreSQL, Flyway, and environment-file checks.
skill.summary: Staged setup workflow for backend, frontend, database, and build verification.
skill.author: Crearize

security_audit.summary: Several static hits are Markdown fence artifacts, not Ruby backtick execution. The real risk is that the skill instructs an agent to run Gradle, pnpm, Docker Compose, Flyway, and development-server commands, which can execute project code and change local services. The environment-file findings are limited to existence checks and report text, with no evidence of secret reading or exfiltration.

remediation.issue: Project setup commands can execute repository-controlled code.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running Gradle, pnpm, Docker Compose, Flyway, or dev-server commands, and show the exact working directory and command first.

remediation.issue: Dependency installation and build steps may trigger lifecycle scripts.
remediation.suggestion: Run the skill only in trusted repositories, review lockfiles and build scripts first, and document when script execution is expected.

remediation.issue: Docker and database migration steps can change local services and data.
remediation.suggestion: Confirm container names, ports, database targets, and migration scope before starting services or applying migrations.

remediation.issue: Environment file checks reference files that may contain secrets.
remediation.suggestion: Keep checks limited to file existence, never print secret values, and state that environment values must stay out of chat logs.

content.value_statement: New project setup often requires coordinated backend, frontend, database, and environment checks. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through a staged setup and verification workflow.
actual_capabilities: Checks installed Java, Node.js, pnpm, Docker, and Docker Compose versions.
Runs backend Gradle wrapper build tasks.
Starts PostgreSQL through Docker Compose and runs Flyway migrations.
Verifies backend and frontend builds and reports setup status.
Checks for expected backend and frontend environment files without reading their contents.
limitations: Assumes a backend, frontend, Gradle, pnpm, Docker Compose, and Flyway project layout.
Does not create missing environment files or populate secret values.
Can run project build scripts and dependency lifecycle scripts, so it should be used only in trusted repositories.
Does not troubleshoot platform-specific installation failures.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Local Backend
use_cases.description: Check Java, enable the Gradle wrapper, build the backend, and apply database migrations for local API work.

use_cases.title: Set Up Frontend Dependencies
use_cases.description: Verify Node.js and pnpm, install frontend packages, and run the frontend build before feature work.

use_cases.title: Validate Onboarding Steps
use_cases.description: Run the staged setup flow and produce a concise status report for team onboarding documentation.

prompt_templates.title: Check My Machine
prompt_templates.prompt: Use setup-dev-env to check whether my machine has the required Java, Node.js, pnpm, Docker, and Docker Compose versions. Do not install anything yet.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up Frontend Only
prompt_templates.prompt: Use setup-dev-env for the frontend target. Confirm before installing dependencies, then report whether the frontend build succeeds.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up Backend And Database
prompt_templates.prompt: Use setup-dev-env for backend and database setup. Show each command before running it, and confirm before starting Docker or applying migrations.

prompt_templates.title: Run Full Verified Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Use setup-dev-env for the full project. Verify tool versions, run backend, frontend, and database steps, then provide a completion report with failures and next actions.

output_examples.output: The skill checks Node.js and pnpm, installs frontend dependencies, runs the frontend build, and summarizes any failures.

output_examples.input: Prepare the backend and database for local development.
output: Gradle build completed or reported with errors.
Migrations completed or reported with the failing step.

output_examples.output: The skill reports installed tool versions, missing prerequisites, expected environment files, and setup steps that still need approval.

best_practices: Review each command and working directory before approving execution.
Use the skill in trusted repositories with reviewed lockfiles and known Docker Compose services.
Keep secret values out of chat and logs when environment files are mentioned.
anti_patterns: Running the full setup in an untrusted repository without reviewing build scripts.
Asking the skill to print environment-file values or copy secrets into the conversation.
Running migrations against shared or production databases.

faq.question: Does this skill install global tools?
faq.answer: No. The documented flow checks tool versions and runs project-level setup commands.

faq.question: Can it create missing environment files?
faq.answer: No. It only checks for expected environment files. Secret values should come from your team's approved process.

faq.question: Which project stack does it expect?
faq.answer: It expects a Java Gradle backend, pnpm frontend, Docker Compose PostgreSQL service, and Flyway migrations.

faq.question: Is it safe for untrusted repositories?
faq.answer: No. Gradle and pnpm commands can execute repository or dependency scripts, so review the project first.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it run automated tests?
faq.answer: The documented backend build excludes tests. The frontend build verifies the application build output.
